targets.title: Decreasing semipositive real-PL regularization
targets.statement:
P02.1 (T3): Decreasing semipositive real-PL regularization
Characterize the higher-dimensional good strict analytic spaces on which every classically psh
function is, near every point, the pointwise decreasing limit of semipositive real PL functions.
The starting function is arbitrary in the classical curve-test class; invariant continuous toric
functions form only a known special case.

reviewed_papers.scope: On strict closed polydiscs over K=k((pi)) with uncountable algebraically closed k, a bounded classical psh boundary-jump function has no local pointwise continuous approximating sequence at the specified boundary point; explicit decreasing Fubini–Study/real-PL and ordinary smooth psh nets still converge. This separates nets from sequences, not general regularization or boundaryless spaces.

earlier_remaining_gaps: This does not characterize all spaces in the atom or establish its full sharp failure range.
The obstruction concerns sequences; it does not refute formulations allowing arbitrary decreasing nets.

Relative-boundary points and a discontinuous starting function are essential to this example; boundaryless higher-dimensional regularization and arbitrary continuous starting functions remain unresolved.
The proof imports the exactly stated Gubler--Rabinoff v2 boundary-extension, classical-pullback, and PL-comparison results; compilation is not independent mathematical verification.

targets.title: Decreasing locally Fubini–Study regularization
targets.statement:
P02.2 (T3): Decreasing locally Fubini–Study regularization
For the same arbitrary classical psh starting class, characterize the spaces admitting local
decreasing approximations by locally Fubini–Study functions. This asks for the Fubini–Study
conclusion itself, rather than merely real-PL or smooth approximation.
earlier_remaining_gaps: Only a partial sequential failure range is established, not a characterization of spaces for arbitrary classical psh functions.
The example admits the requested Fubini--Study nets and therefore is not a counterexample to a net formulation.
Boundaryless spaces, arbitrary continuous noninvariant starting functions, other fields, and general overlap constructions remain unresolved.

targets.title: Decreasing weakly smooth psh regularization
targets.statement:
P02.3 (T3): Decreasing weakly smooth psh regularization
Characterize the higher-dimensional good strict spaces on which every classically psh function
has local decreasing weakly smooth psh approximants. Weak smoothness is deﬁned through
harmonic tropicalizations and must not be identiﬁed with ordinary CLD smoothness.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No complete characterization of the atom is established.
The proof only obstructs sequences; a general weakly smooth net regularization theorem is not proved or refuted.
The boundaryless higher-dimensional problem, arbitrary continuous noninvariant starting class, and harmonic-chart compatibility remain unresolved.

targets.title: Decreasing ordinary CLD-smooth psh regularization
targets.statement:
P02.4 (T4): Decreasing ordinary CLD-smooth psh regularization
Characterize the spaces on which every classical psh function has local decreasing approxima-
tions by ordinary CLD-smooth psh functions. The ordinary smooth requirement is part of
the target; a weakly smooth sequence alone does not solve it.
earlier_remaining_gaps: The full geometric characterization requested in the atom remains open in this report.
The sequential obstruction disappears for the displayed net formulation; it does not establish a sharp failure range for all spaces.
Boundaryless higher-dimensional spaces, arbitrary continuous noninvariant functions, and other base-field geometries are not treated.

targets.title: Classical positivity of regularized local envelopes
targets.statement:
P03.1 (T2): Classical positivity of regularized local envelopes
Find sharp normal or geometrically unibranch higher-dimensional hypotheses under which the
upper-semicontinuous regularization of the local-Fubini–Study/semipositive-real-PL envelope
is classically psh for every upper-semicontinuous obstacle. The perfected-unibranch reduced
strict curve range is already proved. Necessity must account for the branched, nonsplit-node,
and codimension-two pinching obstructions.

reviewed_papers.scope: On the inverse tropicalization of an ordinary open convex domain in a split torus over complete nontrivially valued K, an upper-semicontinuous invariant obstacle with values in R union {-infinity} has the full real-PL/local-Fubini–Study competitor envelope given by its convex-minorant envelope. Noninvariant competitors are allowed. The finite envelope is continuous, classically psh and locally a decreasing ordinary smooth psh limit; the empty case is minus infinity. Every analytic scalar extension commutes. No all-obstacle or all-space classification is proved.

earlier_remaining_gaps: No theorem for arbitrary noninvariant obstacles, even on this smooth torus domain.
No sharp normal or geometrically unibranch higher-dimensional classification or necessity theorem.
No positive conclusion at relative-boundary points of an ambient domain outside the stated boundaryless range.
The argument is an unverified draft; primary GR and CLD theorems are cited inputs, not independently reproved.

semicontinuous obstacle. Classical positivity alone is not the requested conclusion.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No CLD-v2 conclusion for every noninvariant obstacle or arbitrary normal/geometrically unibranch domain.
No sharp additional geometric hypothesis relative to the full classical-positivity atom.
The smooth approximants are not asserted to remain below the obstacle.
This is an unverified draft, with CLD primary definitions and smooth-form calculus as cited inputs.

targets.title: Continuity of local obstacle envelopes

competitor family.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No continuity classification for every finite continuous noninvariant obstacle.
No sharp domain hypotheses in the residual higher-dimensional range.
No guarantee of a finite envelope without a finite convex minorant on unbounded tropical domains.
No theorem on arbitrary nonconvex tropical domains or ambient relative boundary; argument remains an unverified draft.

Continuous revised-CLD psh, classical psh, ordinary CLD smooth and weak smooth classes were not identified.

targets.title: Finite-energy and unbounded local products
targets.statement:
P04.3 (T5): Finite-energy and unbounded local products
Construct a ﬁnite-energy or unbounded extension of the common local product, with an
explicit polar-mass rule. Distinguish a nonpluripolar extension from an extension retaining
polar mass and state the hypotheses under which uniqueness is intended.

reviewed_papers.scope: For summable weighted ideal potentials (y,x^j) on the whole normalized semivaluation link of the smooth complex surface germ, the explicitly defined raw model-intersection measures have a complete atomic limit and a square-tail moment criterion. A rational unbounded example has mass 1/3 and moment 5/3, with no polar mass. A general moment-tail bound, family locality and decreasing continuity, point-blowup refinement invariance, and the exactly normalized coordinate-power identity are proved. No CLD/BFJ identification, named E1 class, canonical polar truncation, or unbounded analytic wedge is claimed.

earlier_remaining_gaps: Full endpoint identification uses the supplied finite common-model theorem; BFJ08 primary text was not available for independent checking.
No singular CLD Bedford--Taylor wedge, canonical nonpluripolar truncation product, or approximation-independence for arbitrary model approximants is constructed.
Locality and decreasing continuity are proved only in the explicit ideal-sum family; finite-map functoriality is checked only for equal coordinate powers.
The raw moment class is not identified with E^1 of an independently fixed theory, and the general atom remains open.

targets.title: Common local products on singular and nonnormal germs
targets.statement:

diﬀerent dimensions and must be compared with their exact boundary normalizers.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No analytic CLD product on the cusp cylinder or conductor descent of wedges is proved.
A link homeomorphism does not establish psh descent, currents descent, or general finite-map functoriality.
No extension to general singular, reducible, or nonnormal germs is constructed.

higher-dimensional real-PA case, and arbitrary nonseparable obstacles remain.

targets.title: An independently geometric singular valuative psh cone
targets.statement:
P12.2 (T4): An independently geometric singular valuative psh cone
On the intrinsic normalized boundary of an excellent singular or nonnormal germ, construct
a valuative psh class with independent geometric meaning and the correct smooth-germ spe-
cialization. Identify its relation to the existing ideal-generated cone. Deﬁning another order-
theoretic completion does not by itself supply that identiﬁcation.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No independent geometric singular cone or comparison with the ideal-generated cone in the full residual scope.
No general smooth-germ specialization beyond the known one-branch curve unit test.
No construction outside the explicitly stated nontrivially valued, strict, disc-normalized, conductor-controlled curve range.

targets.title: An independently geometric singular envelope theory
targets.statement:
P12.3 (T4): An independently geometric singular envelope theory
Construct obstacle envelopes for the independently geometric singular psh cone, establish
their positivity and the appropriate regularity, and compare them with the complete ideal-
psh envelope already known on reduced-curve links.

reviewed_papers.scope: For the explicitly stated disc-normalization/conductor range, the literal radial psh class has the proved clipping supremum. Mixed-zero obstacles have no maximal radial minorant and no order-preserving minorant projection fixing this class. Nodal logarithmic models and primary-gauge cocycles are explicit. The radial classification and earlier nodal failure are known cases; no general singular envelope theory is obtained.

earlier_remaining_gaps: The exact atom asks for a separately constructed geometric singular cone and envelope theory, not this known restricted radial class.
A different nonradial boundary-trace comparison is not excluded; an explicit bounded psh evaluation trace realizes the mixed-zero vector.
No appropriate regularity/positivity theorem for envelopes on arbitrary excellent singular and nonnormal local boundaries.

targets.title: Model-independent bounded singular-local products
targets.statement:
P12.4 (T5): Model-independent bounded singular-local products
Construct bounded mixed Monge–Ampère products on singular and nonnormal normalized
local boundaries, with model independence, the correct intersection comparison, locality and
continuity. The existing compact boundary construction alone supplies no such product.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No independent model-intersection construction, comparison theorem, or conductor-compatible mixed product.
No proof of locality, model independence, or the required monotone-net continuity.
No justified passage of smooth-complex BFJ intersection results to arbitrary excellent/nonreduced-reduction, nonnormal, or positive-characteristic cases.

targets.title: Finite energy on singular local boundaries
targets.statement:
P12.5 (T5): Finite energy on singular local boundaries
Construct an energy functional, ﬁnite-energy class, and its Monge–Ampère calculus for excel-
lent singular and nonnormal germs. Specify reference data, changes of primary gauge, and
the relation between bounded approximation and ﬁnite-energy limits.
earlier_remaining_gaps: Missing reference data, raw mass convention, and geometric products needed for an energy derivative.
No bounded-approximation theorem, capacity estimates, or continuity to finite-energy limits.
Primary-gauge covariance of finite profiles was checked, but no energy change-of-gauge theorem follows.

targets.title: Geometric ﬁnite-map functoriality and conductor descent
targets.statement:
P12.6 (T4): Geometric ﬁnite-map functoriality and conductor descent
Establish compatibility of independently geometric singular psh cones, envelopes and Monge–
Ampère products with ﬁnite maps, normalization and conductor descent. Finite restric-
tion, ideal-cone extrema, normal-domain norm traces, ﬁnite-ﬂat determinant traces and their
tower/gauge rules are known. They do not identify the geometric operators; an unrestricted
continuous degree trace is obstructed.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No geometric finite-map operators on independently constructed local singular cones, envelopes, and products.
Boundary fiber-constancy alone does not establish literal radial analytic descent; conductor/nodal value compatibility is still needed.
Known normal-target traces, finite-flat norms, and continuous conductor criteria do not supply the missing psh or Monge-Ampere comparison theorem.

targets.title: Comparison for nonproportional Reeb polarizations
targets.statement:
P13.1 (T4): Comparison for nonproportional Reeb polarizations
For a normal polarized aﬃne cone (X, T ; ξ) over an algebraically closed trivially valued
characteristic-zero ﬁeld, compare PSH(ξ) and PSH(ξ 0 ) for nonproportional Reeb ﬁelds. Ob-
tain the estimates strong enough for uniform diﬀerentiability of energy. Identities along one
proportional Reeb ray do not answer this question.

reviewed_papers.scope: For the paper’s explicitly defined homogeneous logarithmic-max, finite continuous closure and decreasing-net PSH classes on a positive-dimensional normal affine cone over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, root transport between any two Reeb fields is an intrinsic order isomorphism. It preserves finite maxima and decreasing nets, satisfies the cocycle, and has degree-uniform generator-weight bounds. Raw transport fails to preserve additive constants and addition across polarizations. No identity with an inaccessible book class, energy differentiability, E1 preservation, or mixed-measure result is certified.

earlier_remaining_gaps: No comparison of E_xi(phi) and E_eta(Tphi) or transported mixed measures.
No proof that transport preserves the finite-energy classes.
Supremum-norm bounds are not energy bounds; no uniform differentiability estimate on bounded-energy sets is obtained.
The transport is nonlinear and fails raw compatibility with the quotient by constants.
The exact primary Wu24 definitions and theorems could not be independently audited; the proved theorem uses the explicit definitions stated in the manuscript and inspected local source.
The manuscript and calculations have not received independent mathematical verification.

targets.title: The image of the ﬁxed-Reeb Monge–Ampère operator
targets.statement:
P13.2 (T4): The image of the ﬁxed-Reeb Monge–Ampère operator
Characterize precisely the image of MAξ : E 1 (ξ)/R → M1 (ξ) and the measures admitting a
solution. Retain the invariant carrier X0T and the aﬃne-cone probability normalization. The
operator is already bi-Lipschitz onto its image, so uniqueness there is established; the residual
is the image and existence characterization.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No intrinsic necessary-and-sufficient condition on invariant finite-energy probability measures is established.
Attainment and the required energy/envelope differentiability for the variational functional remain unproved.
Admissible one-sided psh variations yield only an inequality; two-sided continuous-test variations and the Euler--Lagrange implication are missing.
Rational quotient recovery has not been extended with uniform energy and measure control to arbitrary irrational Reeb fields.
The fixed-Reeb external operator theorems are source-described only and were not independently checked at primary-source level.

targets.title: Intrinsic raw-transform image beyond the known regimes
targets.statement:
P14.1 (T4): Intrinsic raw-transform image beyond the known regimes
For a pseudoeﬀective class α on a compact Kähler manifold, intrinsically characterize the im-
age of the perturbation-independent raw ideal-valuative DXZ transform on the MP spectrum.
The full Kähler image and the projective ample rational-line-bundle regime are established.
The big non-nef image remains open; the full real Néron–Severi DXZ–BJ comparison does not
assert the same literal ideal formula outside the rational-line-bundle case.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No new intrinsic positivity class on the MP spectrum for big non-nef generic classes.
No sufficient image criterion, compatible-family reconstruction, or order/approximation comparison in the residual scope.

targets.title: A P-sensitive big non-nef positivity theory
targets.statement:
P14.4 (T4): A P-sensitive big non-nef positivity theory
Construct a positivity theory for big non-nef classes retaining P -singularity data, movable-
positive-part data, or equally informative additional structure. A relatively nef total-space
model cannot represent a non-nef generic class. The raw ideal-valuative transform is only
I-level data and cannot by itself distinguish P -types or recover raw mass.

reviewed_papers.scope: On a specific complex blowup with a big non-nef class, two standard canonical theta-psh potentials have the same complete multiplier-ideal data and the same fixed nonpluripolar products/mass, but different normalized P-envelopes. This is a complex singularity-data obstruction, with no asserted non-Archimedean realization or classification.

earlier_remaining_gaps: No P-sensitive non-Archimedean positivity theory is constructed.
No order, homogeneity, approximation, or DXZ/MP operator comparisons for a proposed realization.
The theorem does not exclude theories retaining richer singularity or birational data.

targets.title: Monge–Ampère measures in the big non-nef realization
targets.statement:
P14.5 (T5): Monge–Ampère measures in the big non-nef realization
Construct the Monge–Ampère measure theory corresponding to a valid big non-nef, P -
sensitive realization, with the correct mass and comparison with existing positive-volume
DXZ and MP operators in their common scopes.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No Monge–Ampère theory on a valid P-sensitive non-Archimedean realization.
No comparison to positive-volume DXZ or MP operators in common scope.
Raw complex measures must not be identified with canonical I-model DXZ measures without a separate theorem.

targets.title: Energy in the big non-nef realization
targets.statement:
P14.6 (T5): Energy in the big non-nef realization
Construct the corresponding intrinsic energy theory and its continuity, diﬀerentiation and
measure compatibility. State which additional singularity data and reference choices it needs;
positive-volume I-level energy alone does not supply a P -sensitive theory.
earlier_remaining_gaps: Additional singularity data and reference choices remain unspecified for a realization.
No continuity, differentiation, or measure compatibility theorem.
The constructed mass-loss potentials are not asserted to belong to any common fixed-reference E1 class.

targets.title: Zero-mass and formal-data reconstruction
targets.statement:
P14.8 (T5): Zero-mass and formal-data reconstruction
Go beyond the established realizable-I-data dichotomy: formulate and solve arbitrary formal-
data realization, a general all-semivaluation reconstruction formula, or the remaining zero-
mass strict-interior reconstruction range with precise admissibility conditions. A canonical
normalized I-model can be recovered from realizable data, but raw representatives and raw
mass cannot descend to the I-quotient. The terminal DXZ left-limit result does not create a
second zero-mass interval.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No realization of arbitrary admissible formal data.
No general all-semivaluation inverse reconstruction formula for DXZ objects.
No remaining strict-interior zero-mass filtration reconstruction range is established.
The parameter s is a complex-potential parameter, not a DXZ filtration level.

targets.title: Path-independent unnormalized zero-volume energy
targets.statement:
P15.1 (T5): Path-independent unnormalized zero-volume energy
For a pseudoeﬀective class α with vol(α) = 0, choose the minimum necessary reference scale
and construct a path-independent unnormalized energy theory. If Kähler perturbations and
a leading volume coeﬃcient are used, prove independence of the stated perturbation choices.
Division by zero volume is not an admissible normalization.

reviewed_papers.scope: For a smooth semipositive zero-volume form on a compact Kähler manifold and smooth admissible potentials, the leading possible coefficient of the unnormalized smooth Aubin–Mabuchi energy has the proved explicit formula. It is independent of smooth Kähler representatives within a fixed auxiliary Bott–Chern class, with first variation, cocycle, monotonicity and concavity. The auxiliary class is retained; no general pseudoeffective, singular, non-Archimedean, or finite-energy completion theorem is proved.

earlier_remaining_gaps: Arbitrary pseudoeffective zero-volume classes need not have the assumed smooth semipositive representative.
The full auxiliary Kahler class eta is retained; independence under changing eta and minimality of the reference are unproved.
Only smooth theta-psh potentials are treated; no finite-energy completion, singular extension, or non-Archimedean inverse-system energy is constructed.
No canonical lower-dimensional carrier is constructed in the general smooth theorem.
The full P15.1 remains open in the catalogue's residual scope.

targets.title: Path-independent zero-volume Monge–Ampère theory
targets.statement:
P15.2 (T5): Path-independent zero-volume Monge–Ampère theory
Construct a path-independent zero-volume Monge–Ampère theory with its carrier, dimension,
mass and reference choices explicitly stated. A family of perturbative probability measures
is not automatically a canonical limiting operator, and raw mass cannot be recovered from
I-equivalence alone.

reviewed_papers.scope: On P^1 x P^1 with a nonzero nef zero-volume class, cohomologous smooth Kähler perturbations with the same leading class-volume coefficient yield different nonzero rescaled top-degree measures on the original carrier. Fibre pushforward removes this particular dependence; a logarithmic-divisor family also distinguishes class-volume order from prescribed-current mass order. These known-type complex product calculations do not settle general carriers, reference minimality, P-data, or any non-Archimedean theory.

earlier_remaining_gaps: A permitted change to the carrier P1 removes this particular measure dependence.
No impossibility theorem rules out richer reference data or a different canonical lower-dimensional carrier.
The calculations do not construct an operator on the general non-Archimedean or transcendental inverse-system space.
Compatibility with arbitrary prescribed P-types, general reference minimality, mass scale and path independence remain unproved.
The full P15.2 remains open in the catalogue's residual scope.

targets.title: P-sensitive lower-dimensional transcendental Okounkov bodies
targets.statement:
P15.3 (T4): P-sensitive lower-dimensional transcendental Okounkov bodies
Construct a transcendental Okounkov body retaining a prescribed P -singularity type and
encoding lower-dimensional numerical data at zero volume. A class-level compact body of
zero ambient volume is already known; it does not identify numerical dimension or retain the
requested P -type.
earlier_remaining_gaps: There is no construction for arbitrary transcendental classes and arbitrary prescribed P-singularity types.
The explicit body is only for one fixed logarithmic divisor, a fixed flag, and an algebraic graded ring; it is not identified with the published limiting partial body.
No general comparison of body dimension or lower-dimensional volume with Cao or class numerical dimension is proved.
No Chebyshev-transform auxiliary-choice independence theorem is proved.
Known catalogue cases and a zero ambient volume identity are not counted as a solution. The full P15.3 remains open.

targets.title: Finite-energy equations on singular or unibranch varieties
targets.statement:
P16.1 (T5): Finite-energy equations on singular or unibranch varieties
Extend the ﬁnite-energy non-Archimedean Monge–Ampère operator and its existence-and-
uniqueness theorem to singular or unibranch varieties, replacing each use of smoothness in
compactness, envelopes, energy diﬀerentiation and comparison. State all retained polarization
and ﬁeld hypotheses.
earlier_remaining_gaps: Descent of the psh cone and semipositive approximants is not proved.
A resolution introduces a big nef nonample class on the source; no equation theorem in that class is supplied.
Compactness, envelopes, first variation, full-mass operator, comparison, and rigidity on the singular space remain unproved.

targets.title: Proper nonprojective algebraizable equation theories
targets.statement:
P16.2 (T5): Proper nonprojective algebraizable equation theories
Construct an appropriate replacement positivity datum and the associated psh, ﬁnite-energy,
comparison and equation theory on proper nonprojective algebraizable spaces. A proper
algebraic scheme with an ample line bundle is already projective, so retaining that datum
while dropping projectivity is not a new case.
earlier_remaining_gaps: A replacement positivity datum and a nonprojective example carrying it are missing.
The associated psh cone, energy, mass, compactness, envelope calculus, operator, and existence/uniqueness are missing.
The cited Stacks statement is catalogue-reported here; its primary page was unavailable.

targets.title: Finite-energy equations in positive residue characteristic
targets.statement:
P16.3 (T5): Finite-energy equations in positive residue characteristic
Construct the required ﬁnite-energy operator and prove existence and uniqueness when the
original residue-characteristic restriction is removed. Replace the resolution, model-regularity
and envelope inputs wherever they are used rather than merely changing the standing ﬁeld
hypothesis.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No unconditional replacements for the required resolution and envelope inputs are proved.
No full finite-energy operator and first-variation theorem in the residual characteristic scope are constructed.
GJKM and FGK source signatures are secondary-reported only; their named primary PDFs were absent from this checkout.
Comparison, rigidity, and existence for the exact atom remain unproved.

targets.title: Finite-energy equations over arbitrary complete valued ﬁelds
targets.statement:
P16.4 (T4): Finite-energy equations over arbitrary complete valued ﬁelds
Extend the operator and existence theorem to nondiscrete valuations and arbitrary complete
non-Archimedean ﬁelds outside the established invariant-toric, skeleton-supported endpoint.
A deﬁnition of the ﬁnite-energy space alone does not establish the operator or the equation.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No mixed finite-energy Monge--Ampere operator outside the established toric skeletal endpoint is constructed.
Approximation independence, mass tails, base-change descent, envelopes, and first variation over arbitrary complete fields are missing.
Existence and uniqueness in the residual scope are missing.
PS23 Remark 4.4 is available only through the catalogue and local secondary packet in this checkout.

targets.title: Finite-energy equations for nonample positivity classes
targets.statement:
P16.5 (T5): Finite-energy equations for nonample positivity classes
Extend the equation theory to big or pseudoeﬀective nonample classes, specifying the psh cone,
reference singularity type, energy and total mass. At zero volume, the existing probability
normalization must be replaced rather than retained unchanged.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No equation theory for a general big nonample class is constructed.
The zero-volume diagnostic does not disprove the existence of every possible replacement positivity or mass convention.
No reference singularity type, corrected zero-volume theory, envelope differentiation, or comparison/rigidity replacement is supplied.
No new narrower equation theorem is claimed; no partial paper is presented.

targets.title: Arbitrary-support ﬁnite-energy measures
targets.statement:
P16.6 (T4): Arbitrary-support ﬁnite-energy measures
Prove the operator and existence-and-uniqueness theorem for arbitrary ﬁnite-energy measure
support beyond the known toric skeletal regime. Measures must satisfy the correct mass and
energy conditions. Do not reduce arbitrary support to a single skeleton or replace the genuine
Monge–Ampère measure by another inverse measure construction.
earlier_remaining_gaps: No arbitrary-support finite-energy existence theorem is established.
A measure approximation would need strong energy control and completion by actual pointwise potentials, not only weak measure convergence.
Attainment of the variational supremum and the integral semicontinuity needed for arbitrary measures are unproved.
The diagnostic remains entirely in the known model/skeletal range and is not counted as new equation progress.

targets.title: Finite-energy equations on nonalgebraizable analytic spaces
targets.statement:
P16.7 (T5): Finite-energy equations on nonalgebraizable analytic spaces
Construct the ﬁnite-energy operator and its existence-and-uniqueness theory on genuinely
nonalgebraizable analytic spaces, with an explicit positivity datum and the necessary com-
pactness, envelope and comparison replacements.




                                              73
earlier_remaining_gaps: An explicit positivity datum on a genuinely nonalgebraizable example is missing.
Global psh compactness, envelopes, energy and total mass, mixed products, and comparison/rigidity are missing.
No descent or gluing theorem establishing existence in this residual scope is supplied.

targets.title: Entropy slopes of arbitrary ﬁnite-energy weak rays
targets.statement:
P19.1 (T5): Entropy slopes of arbitrary ﬁnite-energy weak rays
Prove the remaining entropy-slope statement for arbitrary ﬁnite-energy weak rays on a com-
pact Kähler manifold, outside the stated smooth polarized projective maximal-ray results.
State the non-Archimedean datum, the entropy normalization and the precise ray hypothe-
ses.
earlier_remaining_gaps: Specify and justify the chosen non-Archimedean datum and its relation to an arbitrary, possibly nonmaximal, finite-energy weak ray.
Prove the required mixed-testing asymptotics and entropy upper recovery in the residual scope; the inspected lower bound retains maximality.
Control approximation/time limit interchange without using model-dependent estimates as uniform bounds.

targets.title: Approximation preserving energy, entropy and singularities
targets.statement:
P19.2 (T4): Approximation preserving energy, entropy and singularities
Construct model approximations in the residual hybrid programme that preserve all required
energy, entropy and singularity data. Convergence of energy alone is insuﬃcient, and the
published/source-stated projective Fujita regimes are established subcases.

reviewed_papers.scope: On a fixed flat complex torus and its compact Kähler products, smooth strictly Kähler potentials converge uniformly, in probability-normalized d1 and energy, with unchanged bounded singularity data and any prescribed sequence of finite nonnegative entropies. Additive lifts decrease to zero; a bounded-density example has weak measure convergence and uniform integrability without entropy convergence. Translation averaging erases the entropy defects. These explicit diagnostics do not construct admissible model approximations or refute their existence, and do not solve ray, hybrid-family, or equivariant YTD targets.

earlier_remaining_gaps: Construct admissible algebraic or transcendental model approximations in the residual programme.
Simultaneously preserve prescribed P-singularity/envelope data, energy and entropy rather than merely demonstrate failure for bad smooth sequences.
Supply entropy recovery and the density/reference comparison needed for log-discrepancy-model rays beyond the stated projective Fujita subcases.

targets.title: Hybrid compactness and measures for degenerating families
targets.statement:
P19.3 (T5): Hybrid compactness and measures for degenerating families
Prove the compactness and measure-continuity statements needed along genuinely degener-
ating families of compact Kähler manifolds. A ﬁxed quasi-projective variety hybridized with
explicit scale factors is a diﬀerent known endpoint.
earlier_remaining_gaps: Construct relative compactness for the specified finite-energy potentials on a genuinely degenerating compact family.
Prove family-uniform regularization and identify weak cluster measures as the intended central non-Archimedean Monge--Ampere measure.
Retain compatible positive volume, reference and time-scale normalizations through degeneration; a fixed-variety endpoint or static homeomorphism does not provide them.

targets.title: Equivariant, transcendental and singular hybrid extensions
targets.statement:
P19.4 (T5): Equivariant, transcendental and singular hybrid extensions
Establish the required automorphism-equivariant transcendental and singular extensions, with
the exact stability and metric signatures speciﬁed. Retain the residual distinctions from the
cited smooth polarized projective and static Kähler-class correspondences.
earlier_remaining_gaps: Specify and compare the exact relative stability, automorphism quotient, discrepancy and metric signatures in the residual domain.
Construct genuinely compatible equivariant approximations preserving entropy and singularity data; potential averaging alone fails.
Prove the required transcendental and singular/klt extensions without enlarging smooth polarized projective or static source statements.

targets.title: Bedford–Taylor independence for continuous equal-curvature pairs
targets.statement:
P21.3 (T2): Bedford–Taylor independence for continuous equal-curvature pairs
For a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld and a good separated strict boundaryless pure n-
dimensional analytic space, n ≥ 2, decide whether every positive d0 - and d00 -closed CLD
(p, p)-current, 0 ≤ p ≤ n − 1, has Bedford–Taylor independence on every ordinary open for
continuous psh pairs with equal Hessian currents. The full quantiﬁed equations appear below.
A negative answer must give an analytic counterexample in this scope, not just a defective
abstract tropical pushforward.

reviewed_papers.scope: Over complete nontrivially valued fields, on every ordinary open of a good separated strict boundaryless pure n-dimensional analytic space (n>=2), positive Hessian, residual nefness and CPsh membership are equivalent for actual GJR strict real-PL functions. Zero-current functions annihilate the multiplier for every positive doubly closed target current, as does the stated fixed-neighbourhood locally uniform net closure.

Supporting fixed-domain transfinite compact selection, first-stage collapse for continuous outputs, exact dual test-measure reduction and fixed-current estimate, including trivial valuation. No new universal Bedford--Taylor range or counterexample.

earlier_remaining_gaps: No proof that every continuous equal-Hessian difference satisfies the two-sign CPsh condition or the local harmonic-sum approximation condition.
The geometric harmonic-sum conclusion is restricted to nontrivially valued fields; no corresponding trivial-valuation extension is claimed.

The real-PL consequence depends on the local book's rational-calibration splitting theorem. Its full local proof was read and scope-audited; the GJR primary PDF needed to independently reverify its upstream inputs was not found locally. The core positivity and integral harmonic-sum theorems do not depend on that missing input.
No admissible analytic counterexample was constructed. Coarse tropical defects fail either upstairs curvature equality or closedness under analytic-unit refinement.
No density theorem for arbitrary positive closed currents, arbitrary-current scalar-extension descent, or unrestricted strong/ordinary product comparison was proved.
targets.current_focus: General continuous-pair case returned to backlog.
targets.remaining_full_target: The strict real-PL theorem and supporting dual reduction do not prove the identity for arbitrary continuous equal-curvature psh pairs, including the trivially valued scope.
